- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates in late periods (last 5–10 days) — particularly after sharp spikes — often overshoots true values.
- Shows persistent lag: true values typically rise faster than model forecasts, especially after a dip or low.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after recent highs, then undercorrect upward after lows.
- High sensitivity to recent spikes: model reacts too slowly to sudden price surges, leading to delayed and exaggerated corrections.
- Forecasts for the 30-day horizon often fail to capture the full magnitude of the next-day price movement, especially in the first 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent trends” — when prices spike, model overreacts with a sharp upward bias, then fails to adjust downward as quickly as reality.
- Underestimates volatility in the first 10 days, leading to conservative forecasts that miss early momentum.
- Tends to underestimate the true peak in the 30-day forecast, especially when the true peak occurs in the last 5–10 days.
- Model often fails to account for “rebound” after a sharp drop — underestimates the recovery phase, leading to overly pessimistic mid-forecast values.
